aspects.says: A commit may run again after a crash and can journal nothing, so the outside call it makes must be safe to repeat.
basis: section:15.3 Recovery Aborts What Was Preparing and Commits Again What Was Committing

aspects.says: Join runs its nested participants on new threads, without a timeout, and in 2.1.7 calls commit or abort on all of them whatever they voted.
basis: section:15.7 `Join` Tells Every Nested Participant the Outcome, Joined or Not

aspects.says: The TransactionManager journals each transaction's state and a snapshot of its persistent Context entries, after every participant that does not vote READONLY, in its persistent space, which is in memory unless a disk-backed space is named.
basis: section:15.2 Without a Persistent Space, a Crash Forgets What Was in Flight

aspects.says: A vote is read bit by bit: without PREPARED, a PAUSE or RETRY vote is an abort, and a paused transaction resumes on the abort path.
basis: section:15.4 A Vote Is Read Bit by Bit, and Only `PREPARED` Says Yes

aspects.says: The journal reads persisted keys back as Strings, so an entry persisted under an enum constant breaks the next snapshot or the next start.
basis: section:15.3 Recovery Aborts What Was Preparing and Commits Again What Was Committing
aspects.reason: the failure needs a journal written by one run and read by another; the page shows both outcomes and unit s4 already practises string keys

aspects.says: At start-up, a transaction left preparing is aborted and one left committing is committed again, on every participant of the chain, with only the persisted entries of the last snapshot.
basis: section:15.3 Recovery Aborts What Was Preparing and Commits Again What Was Committing

aspects.says: A paused transaction must be resumed exactly once per pause; an extra resume() is kept and ends the next pause at once.
basis: section:15.6 A Paused Transaction Resumes Once, and an Extra `resume()` Is Kept for the Next Pause
section:15.6.1 Spot the Problem: Resuming on Every Outcome

aspects.says: RETRY runs the transaction again under a new id from the first participant, with no commit or abort for the attempt, and a retry through a persistent journal loses the transient entries.
basis: section:15.5 `RETRY` Starts Over Under a New Id, and Nobody Hears How the First Attempt Ended
